To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the inclusion of a fraction of Hgp from biomass burning (HgBBp) is necessary to better simulate Hg(g) 0 concentrations in the Amazon, 2) HgBBp has a limited effect on global Hg deposition but a significant effect on Hg deposition in northern boreal forests, and 3) the inclusion of HgBBp in global atmospheric models has a significant impact on the distribution of Hg in atmospheric reservoirs.

The inclusion of HgP in BB emission inventories has a limited impact globally on the geographical distribution of total Hg deposition, although locally, the inclusion of Hg in BB emissions has a significant impact on Hg fluxes to ecosystems.

the inclusion of a fraction of Hgerosol from BB in the ECHMERIT model significantly improves the simulation of observed atmospheric HgP levels in the Amazon and that the impact of this fraction on Hg deposition globally is limited, although it is locally significant for boreal and tropical regions where fires are frequent and uncontrolled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the speciation of Hg emissions on Hg deposition.
the impact of the speciation of Hg emitted from BB on the global distribution of Hg.
the impact on atmospheric HgP emissions from BB on Hg deposition, and the factors influencing HgP emissions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion of HgP in biomass burning emissions is important, but that the magnitude of the impact on Hg(g) emissions, and hence on Hg deposition, is limited.
Hg speciation from biomass burning emissions has a limited effect on the overall Hg cycle and global Hg deposition.
the inclusion of HgP in BB emissions has a limited effect on the global scale, but a potentially significant impact in regions of frequent and large fires.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, although Hg(g) emissions from BB dominate Hg deposition to the world’s ocean, HgP from the burning of biomass could be an important source of Hg deposition to terrestrial ecosystems, particularly in northern boreal and tropic forests.

, in order to reduce the uncertainties related to atmospheric Hg modelling, more observations of atmospheric HgP are needed, especially in regions where BB is prevalent, and the speciation of Hg in emissions should be taken into account.
Hg emissions from biomass burning have a significant impact on Hg concentrations and deposition in the global atmosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Hg speciation from BB is important and needs to be taken into consideration in global Hg models and emission inventories.

, in the absence of a reliable estimate of the amount of HgP released from BB, it is essential to include this fraction when modelling Hg emissions from biomass burning in order to correctly represent the Hg budget and its deposition fluxes to the global environment.
the HgP fraction in BB emissions is a major uncertainty in global Hg modelling and needs to be better constrained to reduce uncertainty on Hg atmospheric transport and deposition.
